Self-declared affiliation, 2,775 respondents in this province, which CFPS draws as an independent, self-representative subsample -- one of five provinces (Shanghai, Liaoning, Henan, Gansu, Guangdong) for which the survey supports province-level inference; the other provinces are not written. The 2016 questionnaire asks which religion a person believes in (信仰) where 2012 asked which they belong to (属于), and allows more than one answer, of which the first is counted; shares rose in every province between the two waves, and part of that rise is the wording. Affiliation, not practice.

A survey of adults, not a census: China's census does not ask religion. Self-declared affiliation, 1,839 respondents in this province, which CFPS draws as an independent, self-representative subsample -- one of five provinces (Shanghai, Liaoning, Henan, Gansu, Guangdong) for which the survey supports province-level inference; the other provinces are not written. Weighted by rswt_natcs16, counting the 1,839 respondents who carry it. The same reading of the 2012 file, unweighted, reproduces Table 2 of Lu Yunfeng's report (https://web.archive.org/web/20140809051625/http://iwr.cass.cn/zjwh/201403/W020140303370398758556.pdf) within 0.5 points in every share, which is how the province codes are known to be right; that published table is unweighted, so it and this figure differ by the weight and not by the data. The 2016 questionnaire asks which religion a person believes in (信仰) where 2012 asked which they belong to (属于), and allows more than one answer, of which the first is counted; shares rose in every province between the two waves, and part of that rise is the wording. Affiliation, not practice.
